title: A validity-domain atlas for GPU kernels: conditional certificates, not band-global rules
abstract: A kernel speedup is a point sample presented as a property: it does not say which shapes the advantage survives on, which reference realization scored the pass, or how much tolerance budget the reference already spends. We price all three on a DGX Spark (GB10, sm_120). With rho the reference's own consumption in multiples of the contract budget, an ordinary fp32 matmul reference grows in reduction depth but its pass verdict is a draw, not a threshold: 4/6 seeds pass at K=3608 and 2/6 at K=3632, no seed is monotone, and the fraction re-enters at K=3840. fp32 conv2d is a two-class dispatch surface, not a depth function: a winograd engine at rho 10.195 with 0.52% of elements over budget and bit-identical output under every precision flag a user is told to set, against TF32 tensor-op engines at rho 251.69 with 78.2% over budget that allow_tf32=False removes 99.9% of. At the official L1/40 LayerNorm shape the reference is anchor-clean at rho 0.011 on the benchmark's uniform input but reaches rho 2.529 with 19% of elements over budget at mean/std 1000, where a split-statistics candidate sits at 0.663 and still fails the candidate-versus-reference check. Admission is a binary whole-tensor check against the recorded reference; (rho_max, frac_over) is diagnostic on what a ratio means. Magnitude compresses onto derived coordinates (Spearman 0.986 with the engine class, 0.833 geometry-only) but admission does not (79% bulk accuracy without the class, 100% with it), and the class is only 0.604 predictable against a 0.5625 majority. Over six two-stage chains, end-to-end consumption lands between 0.98x and 2.48x the worse stage; c5 shows two admissible stages (0.0689, 0.6563) composing to 1.2939. On 34 held-out shapes, reduction deliveries are admissible on 9 of 12 at 0.86% cost and conv on none. Five claims were retracted by their pre-registered rules.
change_summary: Round 7 (reissue after the xoD_m6fEALt-e7h5 desk rejection, 2026-10-25T18:19:01Z): carries the one load-bearing measurement absent from the xoD package — the tuple test at commit 34dca87. At fixed shape (C256, k3, s1, d1, H7, W7, batch2) the class flips W<->T on 6/8 consecutive transitions of stride/dilation/pad/layout/batch: class W (stride=1, dil=1, pad<=2) rho_max 6.4-6.8, frac_over 0.004-0.005, bit-identical under every precision flag; class T (stride=2 or dil=2) rho_max 315.1-369.4, frac_over ~0.78, allow_tf32=False removes 99.9% (ratios 0.0016/0.0022/0.0007). The boundary is a step function of the tuple (not a smooth surface) and the engine class is a fitted label (0.604 vs 0.5625 majority); section 2.5 records the full 9-row grid and the tuple that drives each class, and results/tuple_test.json ships every rho/frac_over with its per-row tuple. The dispatcher's (C, output extent) rule misclassifies one H step on the 1x1 family (C16/C64 implicit_convolve_sgemm rho 0.005-0.032; C256 cutlass_80_tensorop_s1688gemm rho 141-184). The S56 contract table stays corrected (conv 0/4 admissible at 94-197; reduction 9/12 admissible, +0.86% over passing rows, +3.53% SE 1.37 over all 24, conv delivery claim withdrawn). All 41 cited artifacts verified by s50-s54; s54 audit 6/6; package 137 files, expanded 1.93MB < 2MB cap.
